title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills are due today.  For those who pay after today you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you did not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: DISASTER DECLARATION
full_story:
Gov. JB Pritzker on Tuesday issued a state disaster proclamation for eleven counties ravaged by severe weather this spring and early summer.

The proclamation covers Kankakee, McLean, Stephenson and Winnebago counties for severe weather events that took place in March and April; and Coles, Cook, Effingham, Jefferson, LaSalle, Warren and Woodford counties for storm events over the past month.

It comes amid a record stretch of severe weather in the Land of Lincoln. Midway through the year, the National Weather Service has already confirmed 173 tornadoes in Illinois, the most recorded in a single year.  Several communities have also sustained damage from flooding, hail and straight-line winds.

“Illinois has faced unprecedented severe weather this year, and I remain committed to supporting every community, business, and family as they rebuild,” Pritzker said in a statement.  “As communities recover, we remember the lives that were lost and hold their families and loved ones in our thoughts during this difficult time.”

Pritzker is scheduled to visit Effingham and Jefferson counties today.  An EF-3 tornado ripped through the area on June 17th, injuring two people and damaging dozens of structures.  He surveyed damage in Coles County earlier this month after an EF-2 tornado hit.

The proclamation frees up additional state resources and personnel for response and recovery operations and can facilitate requests for state and federal disaster relief.

Communities in impacted counties, for example, can now apply for up to $250,000 through the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Disaster Response program to assist with cleanup, debris removal and public infrastructure repairs.

Pritzker said last week that he expects the state to seek additional federal assistance for the June tornadoes, either through the Federal Emergency Management Agency or Small Business Administration, though state officials are still working with local officials to assess damage and determine whether it meets eligibility for federal assistance programs.

title: JULY BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
ImpactLife will have a blood drive tonight at the Iuka Fire Protection District from 4 to 7 pm.  Then there will be another blood drive at the Clay County Hospital on Thursday, July 9th from 10 am to 1 pm.  To schedule an appointment at either of these drives go to https://login.bloodcenter.org/donor/schedules/drive_schedule/144076

The American Red Cross is also making an urgent call for blood donors to book an appointment to give now to ensure hospitals stay ready to help patients without delay.

There will be a blood drive Friday, July 10th from 1 to 5 pm at the Clay County Health Department.  All donors who donate blood during this drive will get a American Red Cross Looney Tunes T-shirt.  Then there will be a Blood Drive at the Flora Oddfellows Lodge on Friday July 24th from 1 to 5 pm.  Donors at this drive will get a Fandango Movie Reward by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  You can make an appointment to donate at Red Cross Blood Drives by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  Save time with RapidPass.  Complete your pre-donation reading and health history at RedCrossBlood.org/RapidPass or with the Blood Donor App before your appointment.

title: CCH SPORTS PHYSICALS
full_story:

title: NASHVILLE COACH CHARGED
full_story:
Attorney General Kwame Raoul charged a baseball coach at Nashville Community High School with criminal sexual assault and aggravated criminal sexual abuse.

54-year-old Chad Malawy of Nashville was charged in Washington County Circuit Court with one count of Class 1 felony criminal sexual assault, punishable by up to 15 years in prison, and one count of Class 1 felony aggravated criminal sexual abuse, punishable by up to 15 years in prison.  Malawy was also charged with two Class A misdemeanor counts of solicitation to obstruct justice and two Class A misdemeanor counts of attempted obstruction of justice.  Malawy is currently detained in the Washington County jail.

The charges stem from an investigation by Raoul’s office and the Nashville Police Department.  The Illinois State Police (ISP) assisted with forensics.

Officials encourage residents with additional information to submit a tip by calling Special Investigator Cloee Frank at 217-843-0347.

“Criminal sexual assault is a heinous and indefensible crime,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly. “ISP crime scene investigators will use every tool available to ensure those perpetrating these crimes are held accountable.”

Assistant Attorney General Sarah Holst Schryer is prosecuting the case for Raoul’s office.

The public is reminded that the defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

title: IPRB SUMMER TEACHERS PROGRAM
full_story:
Thirty-six Illinois educators completed the 16th IPRB Summer Teachers Program last week.  The program included an oil lifecycle field trip – including a drill site, two active production sites, an oil storage and transportation facility located at the Patoka tank farm and a CountryMark refinery tour.

Teachers also participated in learning stations and watched presentations by industry professionals and academics covering Illinois geology, wellsite geology, hydraulic fracturing, drilling and producing, oil and gas careers, land and legal aspects of the industry, coring, drill stem testing, drilling mud, seismic mapping, subsurface fluid migration and much more.  Teachers participated in oil-and-gas focused educational workshops featuring classroom lessons and activities included in Illinois State Board of Education-approved curriculum, in addition to taking home oil-and-gas focused classroom activity kits.

title: HOLIDAY TRAVEL
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation, the Illinois State Police and local law enforcement throughout the state are reminding the public: Whether you’re drinking alcohol, using cannabis or under the influence of other drugs, if you get behind the wheel, you’ll face the consequences.  During the Fourth of July “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” campaign, zero tolerance will be shown for those driving impaired.

“Driving impaired is not a game, it’s a decision with potentially deadly consequences,” said Stephane B. Seck-Birhame, IDOT’s bureau chief of Safety Programs and Engineering.  “Plan ahead.  If you’re drinking alcohol, using cannabis or any other drug, don’t drive.  Designate a sober driver, call a ride service or stay put.”

According to provisional IDOT data, last year in Illinois during the Independence Day holiday from 6 pm Friday to 11:59 pm Monday, there were 17 fatal crashes resulting in 18 fatalities, an average of more than five people killed each day.  Four of the 17 fatal crashes involved drivers who had been drinking, resulting in four of the 18 fatalities.

In addition to removing impaired drivers from the roads, police will strongly enforce seat belt, speeding and other traffic laws through Monday.  Wearing a seat belt is the law in Illinois and your best defense against impaired drivers.  Always buckle up and make sure your passengers do, too.

“If you’re driving to watch fireworks, attend a picnic or celebrate the 250th anniversary of the birth of our nation some other way, remember to drive safely,” said ISP Division of Patrol Col. Christopher Owen.  “Wear your seat belt, watch your speed, and don’t drive distracted or impaired.”

The Independence Day “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” campaign is funded with federal highway safety tax dollars administered by IDOT and runs through the early morning hours of Monday.  The effort is administered by IDOT with federal funds and coincides with the comprehensive multimedia campaign “It’s Not a Game.”

title: FERTILIZER TARIFFS SUSPENDED
full_story:
An executive order by President Donald Trump this week temporarily lifted countervailing duties on phosphate fertilizer imports from Morocco through early next year.

American Farm Bureau Federation (AFBF) President Zippy Duvall said farmers applaud the action.

“Skyrocketing fertilizer costs have contributed to rising expenses for farmers who were already struggling after years of inflation, depressed commodity markets and high interest rates,” Duvall said, who noted 7 out of 10 farmers in a recent AFBF survey indicated they would not be able to afford enough fertilizer this season.

USDA analysis indicates American farmers could save approximately $1.82 billion annually through lower phosphate fertilizer costs as additional supplies enter the US market.  The action is expected to reduce phosphate fertilizer prices by approximately 22%, benefiting more than 100,000 farms across 97 million planted acres nationwide.

“The decision to suspend tariffs on critical supplies, along with the recent request for emergency economic aid for farmers, are common-sense steps that will bring relief to farmers at a time when they need it most,” Duvall said.

title: FIREWORKS SAFETY
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) is reminding organizations and individuals sponsoring fireworks displays in Illinois to be sure their fireworks vendor has the required state licenses and certificates issued by IDNR and the Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) before their fireworks show.

The Illinois Explosives Act requires that anyone who purchases, possesses, uses, transfers, stores or disposes of explosives, including display fireworks, must have an explosives license and explosives storage certificate issued by the IDNR.

Licensing and storage requirements administered by the IDNR do not apply to consumer fireworks (classified as 1.4 explosives).  Approved consumer fireworks are regulated by the OSFM and are permitted only in villages, counties and municipalities that have passed ordinances allowing such displays.  Consumer fireworks may be purchased and displayed only by adults who have obtained permits from their local jurisdiction. Handheld fireworks, including firecrackers, roman candles and bottle rockets, are not approved for sale or use in Illinois.

Anyone possessing, using, transferring or purchasing display fireworks without a valid IDNR individual explosives license or storage certificate is violating Illinois law and could incur penalties.  A violation of the Illinois Explosives Act can be a Class 3 felony, with a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $10,000 fine.  In addition, IDNR can assess administrative fines for violations involving display fireworks and other explosives.

According to the National Fire Protection Association fireworks started 32,302 fires in 2023, including 3,760 structure fires, 849 vehicle fires, 27,252 outside fires, and 441 unclassified fires.  These fires caused an estimated 15 civilian deaths, 58 civilian injuries and $142 million in direct property damage.  These fires are not only caused by commercial/consumer fireworks, but also by unregulated novelty fireworks that are sometimes purchased at local supermarkets.

In addition to fireworks, novelties such as sparklers, snappers, and poppers are dangerous.  Sparklers account for the greatest number of fireworks injuries, and often to the youngest victims.  Sparklers burn hotter than 1,200 degrees; hot enough to melt many metals and turn steel glowing red.  An instantaneous touch of this will cause a burn and may result in permanent damage or scarring.

“Each July Fourth, thousands of people, many of them children and teens are injured while using consumer fireworks,” said Illinois State Fire Marshal Michele Pankow.  “Far too often, people underestimate the dangers associated with fireworks.  What may seem like a harmless celebration can quickly result in devastating burns, serious injuries, fires, and even death.  We encourage everyone to leave fireworks to the professionals and make safety a priority this Independence Day.
